rows.subtype: Clipped and halting speech at work [Interpreting]
rows.description: A colleague who suddenly becomes clipped or halting in meetings may be stressed, unsure or holding back disagreement. A private, unhurried check-in is wiser than concluding hostility.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Measured voice in delivering hard news [Regulating]
rows.description: A young manager or clinician delivering bad news uses a slow, measured pace and clear sentences so the listener can take it in. Rushing through it to end the discomfort tends to sound cold.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: In some Indian and other group settings overlapping speech signals engagement, while in others it signals disrespect. A young professional watches the local norm before judging someone as rude or passive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young parent sings lullabies to a baby to soothe, bond and share family and cultural songs. Even a tired, off-key voice works because presence and warmth matter more than skill.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Greetings range from namaste, salaam, bows and handshakes to cheek kisses; the same gesture can seem warm or overly familiar. A young adult follows the other person's lead and asks when unsure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Saying goodbye and taking leave at work [Regulating]
rows.description: A young professional taking leave from a meeting or job says thanks, signals when to end, and leaves doors open. Vague or abrupt exits can damage relationships, while warm closure keeps trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult telling personal stories decides how much to share with whom. Sharing builds closeness, but oversharing with strangers or online may cause regret, so context and consent matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional gives a short summary first, then details, and clarifies jargon for mixed audiences. Too much detail can hide the point, while too little can leave people unprepared.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young professional confirms decisions in writing with a line like just to confirm we agreed. It reduces mistakes, though repeating too often may signal distrust to a colleague.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Asking in cultures with indirect style [Mismatch]
rows.description: In some cultures direct questions feel blunt and people prefer indirect hints or asking through a third person. A young adult adapts, watching for softeners and silence that mean no.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
